method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Compilation No. 81, compilation date 1 July 2026, includes amendments up to Act No. 16, 2025 (register id C2026C00260)
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted statutory text is reproduced under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution in ../../SOURCE-LICENSE.md

checks.command: l4 run cea-cases-candidate.l4 ; l4 run cea-cases-elector.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: the elector: ss 4(1) (elector), 93, 99(1)-(2), 100, 101 (enrolment, transfer, change of address, the offences and bars), 245 (compulsory voting, the penalty notice, the $20, the offences); the candidate: ss 163-166, 170, 172, 173 (the $2,000 deposit, returned at 4%), 175, 287(9), 289(2), 294 (funding, indexed amounts as inputs), 310A (candidate return); Constitution s 44 a borrowed fact
seat: the elector (enrolment, compulsory voting, the failure-to-vote penalty) and, standing for Parliament, the candidate (nomination, deposit and its return, eligibility as far as the Act states it)
